title: Restriction of Picard groups across a finite boundary
statement: Let $C$ be a smooth affine connected curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ [def-sc-curves], let $C\hookrightarrow\overline C$ be a smooth proper connected compactification [lem-sc-compactification], and let $S=\overline C\setminus C$. Then restriction of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] defines a surjective homomorphism on Picard groups [def-sc-picard-group] $\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ whose kernel is the subgroup generated by the classes $[P]=[\mathcal O_{\overline C}(P)]$ for $P\in S$. After choosing $P_0\in S$ and splitting degree by $[P_0]$, this identifies the induced map $\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)/\langle[P]-[P_0]:P\in S\rangle\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ (with $\operatorname{Pic}^0$ as in [def-sc-pic0]) with an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use [lem-sc-pic-restriction-exact] to obtain surjectivity of the specified Picard pullback and identify its kernel with the closure of the boundary point classes.

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, restriction and boundary divisors

proof.text: Use [def-sc-pic0], implemented by Scheme.picDegreeHom and Scheme.coe_ker_picDegreeHom, and Scheme.picDegreeHom_ofClosedPoint: each closed boundary point has degree one. For a chosen boundary point p define sigma(n)=p^n and q(x)=x/sigma(deg x). In Lean prove deg(sigma(n))=n, deg(q(x))=0, r(q(x))=r(x) because r(p)=1, and q restricts to the identity on ker(deg). Hence t=r restricted to ker(deg) is surjective.

proof.text: Set G=ker(deg) and Lambda=ker(t). Prove by membership in mapped subgroups that map(G.subtype,Lambda)=map(q,ker r). Rewrite the latter using the boundary kernel and MonoidHom.map_closure. Since every boundary point has degree one, q maps the boundary generators exactly to the differences [P]/[P0], proving the required generator equality.

proof.text: Apply QuotientGroup.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective to t. Its value on each QuotientGroup.mk L is definitionally t L=r L.val, giving the required compatibility with the actual Picard restriction.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.Hom.pic_restriction_boundary {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C] (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g] [hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 c.g] : Function.Surjective (Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i) ∧ (Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i).ker = Subgroup.closure {L | ∃ P : closedPoints c.Z, P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base ∧ L = @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P} ∧ ∀ (P₀ : closedPoints c.Z), P₀.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base → ∃ (G : Subgroup c.Z.Pic) (_ : (G : Set c.Z.Pic) = c.g.picZero) (Λ : Subgroup G), Subgroup.map G.subtype Λ = Subgroup.closure {L | ∃ P : closedPoints c.Z, P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base ∧ L = @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P / @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P₀} ∧ ∃ e : (G ⧸ Λ) ≃* C.Pic, ∀ L : G, e (QuotientGroup.mk L) = Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i L.val
